doc.title: Statements
doc.paragraph: Adaptive Script allows you to execute one or more statements, sequentially. Statements are separated by the ; character. This programmatic flow lets the programmer write logic procedurally. The following is a list of the statements that are available in Adaptive Script.

section.title: Block
section.paragraph: A Block is a sequence of statements that are executed sequentially. When creating a script, a new block is created initially. Blocks can be nested inside existing blocks, using braces { }.

section.title: Example
Assignment
section.paragraph: The Assignment statement assigns the value of an Expression to an AssignmentExpression. An AssignmentExpression is also an Expression which must evaluate to one of the following:
This flexibility allows us to support a popular technique of assignment known as "destructuring". In destructuring, we assign an object or list into multiple variable names in one assignment.

section.title: Break
section.paragraph: The break statement breaks out of the current block.

section.title: Call
section.paragraph: A Call statement is an evaluation that compiles to the call of an Adaptive Value.

section.title: Const
section.paragraph: The const statement declares constant variables.

section.title: Do While
section.paragraph: The do-while statement executes a block of statements until a condition is met. Unlike the while statement, the do-while statement executes at least once.

section.title: Example
For
section.paragraph: The for statement executes a block of statements until a condition is met. Unlike the while statement, the for statement executes an initializer, a condition, and an incrementor.

section.title: Example
Function
section.paragraph: This declares a function. Parameters may be simple names or the same list and object Patterns used in let / const destructuring (holes, defaults, rest, rename, nesting, string keys, and [expression] computed keys). Parameter defaults may be any Expression. Types may be written on simple parameters, on Pattern leaves, and on a whole Pattern formal (for upcoming compile-time checking). When a Pattern parameter is optional, supply a whole-argument default such as = {} so the Pattern has an object to bind.
The same Patterns are already available in assignment, for-of heads, and C-style for initializers. Calls may use argument spread f(...array) to expand an array into separate arguments.

section.title: Example
If
section.paragraph: The if statement executes a block of statements if a condition evaluates to true.

section.title: Interface
section.paragraph: Declares a named object shape for script type checking. Optional properties use ?; use extends for one or more bases. See for syntax, examples, and checking flags.

section.title: Example
Let
section.paragraph: The let statement declares a local variable.

section.title: Return
section.paragraph: The return statement returns a value from a block of execution.

section.title: Example
Switch
section.paragraph: The switch statement branches control flow based on the value of an expression and the value of each case.

section.title: Example

section.paragraph: Unlike the switch in ECMAScript, Adaptive Script includes an optional syntax that allows you to specify a matching function through the using option. The function provided must take two values and return a boolean result. You may use any built-in Adaptive Function, or provide a custom function, written in Adaptive Script.
section.title: Example
Type
section.paragraph: Declares a local type alias: type Name = Type;. See for the type expression grammar, railroad diagrams, and checking flags.

section.title: Example
section.code: type Id = integer; const x: Id = 3;

section.title: While
section.paragraph: The while statement executes a block of statements until a condition is met. Unlike the do-while statement, the while statement executes the condition first and may not execute the block at all.
